title: Petrov's Defense: the Damiano trap
line: Taking back the pawn on e4 too soon lets the white queen come out, and one more slip loses yours.

steps.text: Petrov's Defense: White's knight has taken your pawn on e5.
Say you take back on e4 at once, as about one club player in ten does. The queen attacks your knight, and your king stands behind it.
If the knight steps away, the file opens: the white knight jumps off with check from the queen and attacks your queen. That is the trap.
Back to the queen move. Block the file with your queen: she also guards the knight.

wrong.e4f6: That is the trap you just saw: the knight jumps off with check and attacks your queen.

steps.after: White takes your knight. The white knight on e5 now stands between the two queens.

steps.text: Attack the knight with a pawn. If it steps away, your queen takes White's.
steps.after: White guards the knight with a pawn.

steps.text: Take the knight. That gets back the piece you lost on e4.
steps.after: Material is level, but White has the freer game. That small edge is what taking at once cost.

steps.text: Back to the start of the trap. The safe way: chase the knight first.
Push the pawn in front of your queen one square to attack the knight.
steps.after: The knight steps back. Now the pawn on e4 can be taken safely.

summary: Before taking back, look at the file your king stands on. Chase the knight first, then take.
